response.query: Propose two candidate prospective designs (pivotal reader and clinical-utility): primary/secondary endpoints, sample-size estimates, success criteria, and clinical-impact metrics.
response.answer: Two designs: pivotal reader uses primary endpoint HbA1c reduction; clinical-utility design focuses on secondary endpoint patient-reported outcomes. Sample size: pivotal 300; clinical-utility 500. Success criteria: pivotal meets HbA1c target; clinical-utility shows significant improvement in quality of life.

results.title: Insulin Therapy | Type 2 Diabetes
results.content: In clinical trials enrolling adult patients with T2D, the glucose-lowering effect of once-daily Basaglar U-100 plus OADs was compared with that of once-daily insulin glargine U-100 products plus OADs. Patients were either insulin-naïve and had failed to achieve glycemic control while on at least two OADs or were already using an insulin glargine U-100 product plus at least two OADs, with or without adequate glycemic control. A total of 343 patients with T1D (A1C above 7% and below 10%, on once-daily basal insulin and rapid-acting insulin analogs for at least one year) were randomized (1:1) to receive either insulin glargine U-300 (172 patients) or insulin degludec U-100 (171 patients). * In patients with T2D switching from a regimen of only a once- or twice-daily basal insulin, Ryzodeg 70/30 should be initiated at the same dose and injection schedule.
